correctness.rationale: Let G=S_k×S_k act on k-subsets of a disjoint union of two k-blocks. Its vertex orbits O_i have i points in the first block. The minimal intersection over O_i×O_j is |i+j−k|, so their maximal Johnson graph distance is k−|i+j−k|; singleton endpoints are also compatible. An orbit supports a fixed-point barycenter exactly when |2i−k|≥t=k−r. Fixed points in a geometric simplex have orbit-constant barycentric coefficients, yielding the exact orbit-barycenter simplicial model rather than a fixed-vertex or invariant-homology surrogate. For 0≤r<k the admissible indices split into low/high blocks of length m=⌊r/2⌋+1, and incompatible low/high orbit pairs are precisely |i−j|<t, the bipartite band graph F_{m,t}. Standard independence-complex neighborhood containment folds remove t−1 low vertices then t−1 high vertices per block, retaining a disjoint edge and F_{m−t,t}. Iteration leaves b=ceil(m/t) disjoint edges, whose independence complex is a join of b copies of S0, hence S^{b−1}=S^{floor(r/[2(k−r)])}. At r≥k the full Rips simplex is G-stable and its fixed set contractible. We independently enumerated all orbit pair extrema for k=1..7 and checked selected exact graph fold sequences; they corroborate but do not establish the all-k proof.
residual_risks: General geometric fixed-point triangulation assumes the finite group action permutes vertices simplicially; satisfied here.
Finite checks cannot replace the all-parameter fold proof; homology calculation alone would not establish homotopy.

value.rationale: The theorem determines geometric fixed-space homotopy at every Rips scale for the canonical equal two-block Young subgroup of J(2k,k) over all k, with arbitrarily high-dimensional sphere stages and the final contractibility threshold. Its exact orbit-barycenter reduction and explicit band-graph folds are a reusable structural tool; ambient Rips homology or characters alone cannot recover geometric fixed loci. This is a motivated natural equivariant topological classification, not a synthetic finite enumeration.
